provenance: 2026-07-20 structural-dark row 2 CLOSED (RNS leg). send_to_rns used to return a bare bool that collapsed five outcomes -- not_connected, no_lxmf_source, circuit_open, no_path and a real send_error -- into one False, so the mesh oracle's RNS leg (bool(send_to_rns(...))) filed a genuine send crash in its BENIGN bucket and oracle_delivery_degraded under-counted real failures. Cure: RnsSendResult (frozen dataclass with __bool__, so every truthiness call site is unchanged) plus a .reason the responder records into the audit log. Two traps this case guards: (1) reading a SHRINKING benign_rns_ambiguous as fewer failures -- it measures what we cannot TELL APART, so it falls because reasons are now named, not because delivery improved; the real-failure count can rise at the same time and that is the fix working. (2) assuming a named benign reason (no_path/circuit_open) is a failure -- it stays excluded from the confirmable failure set; only send_error is a failure. Deliberate non-port: MeshAnchor's bridge_send_mixin is diverged (no bounded_call/_on_wedge machinery) and has no bridge_rns_events_mixin, so it has no consumer for the richer result.

provenance: 2026-07-20 structural-dark row 5 CLOSED. The AREDN organ had two watchers and both required a STATEMENT the operator had to remember to make: aredn_node_ips in map_settings.json (configured-source legs) or organ_expectations.aredn in deployment.json (role-aware leg, 2026-07-19). So the 2026-06-12 origin state -- the AREDN-site box found with its organ silently dormant while every 'AREDN' node on the map came from the worldmap fallback -- was STILL undetectable on a box that was never configured and never declared. probe_aredn_organ_undeclared closes it with positive evidence only: localnode.local.mesh resolves (it cannot without an AREDN node serving DNS on that LAN) AND that address answers sysinfo, while the box has neither statement. Measured 2026-07-20: resolves on the AREDN-site box to exactly its configured node IP; does not resolve on a same-fleet box with no AREDN path. Three traps this case guards: (1) trying to close the row by absence -- 'no declaration' cannot distinguish a forgotten organ from a box that has no AREDN anywhere near it, which is why the detector waits for a node to answer rather than for a config to be missing; (2) reading a silent probe as 'no AREDN organ exists' -- a box with no AREDN LAN is correctly invisible because there is nothing to observe, not because it was checked and cleared; (3) expecting a page -- it is escalation-only by seed policy, since an unadopted organ is lost coverage rather than an outage and has by construction already been that way a long time. Companion fix: an ABSENT map_settings.json used to collapse into the same 'unreadable' as a corrupt one, so the probe returned indeterminate BEFORE the declaration leg and wiping the whole settings file -- the strongest form of the wipe class -- was invisible on a declared box.

input.question: A fleet box shows no aredn_organ_undeclared signal and no AREDN nodes on its map. Does that mean its AREDN organ is fine, and how would we know if a box at an AREDN site had simply never been configured?
